newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin "alert" but should take it easy - Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin "alert" but should take it easy - Kohl.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin has made a good comeback from heart surgery and was alert and energetic on Saturday, said German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, the first Western leader to see the president since his operation in November.
But Kohl said the Russian president's quintuple bypass operation on November 5 had been a major challenge, including mentally, and he advised Yeltsin to take things easy.

The Kremlin leader looked wan and tired in television film of Kohl's arrival for three hours of talks at the Rus hunting lodge near Moscow. But he seemed pleased to see the chancellor, whom he sees as a personal friend and last met in September.
At a news conference after the meeting, Kohl was clearly reluctant to discuss Yeltsin's health.

Asked whether the 65-year-old Yeltsin would continue to be dogged by problems of old age, he said: "This is a difficult question. Yeltsin has had many challenges and much to overcome in 1996. Heart problems have also psychological effects -- you do not shed these off very easily."
"But he has come back well from the operation and has started working again," the chancellor added. "He should be sensible and take it easy a little longer."
Yeltsin seemed to have plenty of energy for his task, Kohl said, and was mentally alert.
"During our meeting he had very little paper with him, he talked alertly about the subjects and dicussed them in a concrete way," he said.

At their last meeting, at Rus on September 7 two days after Yeltsin announced he needed surgery, Kohl said Yeltsin was "fully active". Kremlin doctors have since said the president was very limited by his illness.
The president returned to his desk a fortnight ago but has scarcely been seen in public and has made only brief television appearances.
